subs.label: Comedy Series
subs.axis: Axis: by comic engine and form: the domestic and workplace sitcom first, then friends, romance, youth and place, character and embarrassment, documentary and absurd forms, sketch, satire and parody, music and sport, the fantastic genres, crime and darkness; comedy-drama and tragicomedy last

leaves.label: Family Sitcom
leaves.defn: A studio (multi-camera, audience or laugh-track) sitcom whose comic engine is the family household: parents, children and relatives colliding at home (Father Knows Best, All in the Family, The Cosby Show, Everybody Loves Raymond). A single-camera family comedy goes to B8-2; a family comedy-drama goes to B8-24.
leaves.aliases: domestic sitcom; family sitcom; multi-camera family sitcom
leaves.see: B8-2 Single-Camera Family Comedy; B8-24 Comedy-Drama; B10-4 Teen Sitcom
leaves.axis: by the family at the centre: the classic nuclear household first, then class, community, family shape and generations; period nostalgia last

leaves.label: Single-Camera Family Comedy
leaves.defn: A family sitcom shot single-camera without audience or laugh track, playing family life with filmic cutaways, narration or deadpan (Malcolm in the Middle, The Middle, Friday Night Dinner, Fresh Off the Boat). A studio family sitcom goes to B8-1; a family mockumentary such as Modern Family goes to B8-11.
leaves.see: B8-1 Family Sitcom; B8-11 Mockumentary; B8-24 Comedy-Drama
leaves.axis: by the family at the centre: the nuclear household first, then class, family shape and generations; period nostalgia last

leaves.label: Workplace Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose comic engine is a workplace and its colleagues, the job supplying the situation and the hierarchy the conflict (The Mary Tyler Moore Show, Cheers, The IT Crowd, Superstore). A workplace mockumentary goes to B8-11; a military unit to B8-4; a political office to B8-15.
leaves.see: B8-4 Military Comedy; B8-11 Mockumentary; B8-15 Political Satire
leaves.axis: by the workplace: office first, then media, service trades, public service, hospitals, schools; the church last

leaves.label: Military Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series set in an army unit, camp or wartime posting, its humour drawn from rank, drill and the absurdities of war (Dad's Army, Hogan's Heroes, M*A*S*H, Bluestone 42). A satire of the military establishment as policy goes to B8-15.
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Hangout Sitcom
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is a group of friends, flatmates or neighbours simply spending time together, plot subordinate to banter (Seinfeld, Friends, How I Met Your Mother, The Golden Girls). A group defined by a job goes to B8-3; one built around a romance to B8-6.
leaves.aliases: friends sitcom; ensemble sitcom; hangout comedy
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; B8-6 Romantic Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by the bond: friend groups first, then shared homes and odd couples, slacker gangs; older friends last

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy Series
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is a couple or the search for love: courtship, cohabitation, dating and break-ups (Mad About You, Catastrophe, The Mindy Project, Nobody Wants This). A marriage played as family life goes to B8-1/B8-2; a romance-led drama to B1.
leaves.see: B8-1 Family Sitcom; B8-5 Hangout Sitcom; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by the stage of love: established couples first, then dating and singles; anthologies of love stories last

leaves.label: Teen Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series about adolescents or students made for a general or adult audience, built on school, sex and growing up (The Inbetweeners, Derry Girls, PEN15, Community). A teen sitcom made for children's networks goes to B10-4.
leaves.aliases: high-school comedy; college comedy; coming-of-age comedy
leaves.see: B10-4 Teen Sitcom; B10-5 Teen Drama; B8-24 Comedy-Drama
leaves.axis: by the institution: high school first, college and university second

leaves.label: Rural Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is country or small-town life, often with the rube-versus-city contrast (The Andy Griffith Show, Green Acres, Corner Gas, Letterkenny). A small-town comedy-drama goes to B8-24.
leaves.aliases: rural sitcom; rube sitcom; village comedy
leaves.see: B8-24 Comedy-Drama; B8-1 Family Sitcom

leaves.label: Character Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series built on one grotesque, deluded or hapless central character whose flaw drives every plot (Fawlty Towers, Keeping Up Appearances, Mr. Bean, One Foot in the Grave). Where the comedy is the audience's embarrassment rather than the character, see B8-10.
leaves.see: B8-10 Cringe Comedy; B8-13 Sketch Comedy
leaves.axis: by the flaw: the pompous and aspirational first, then the hapless and accident-prone; losers, schemers and grumps last

leaves.label: Cringe Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is social embarrassment, the awkward pause and the faux pas, often with the star playing a version of himself (Curb Your Enthusiasm, Peep Show, Extras, I'm Alan Partridge). A documentary-style cringe comedy goes to B8-11.
leaves.see: B8-11 Mockumentary; B8-9 Character Comedy

leaves.label: Mockumentary
leaves.defn: A scripted comedy series shot as if it were a documentary or reality show, with talking heads and camera awareness (The Office, Parks and Recreation, Summer Heights High, What We Do in the Shadows).
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; B8-16 Parody Series
leaves.axis: by the documentary subject: the workplace first, then a character or celebrity, a pastiche of documentary and reality TV; family and community last

leaves.label: Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.defn: A narrative comedy series whose engine is the illogical, dreamlike or anti-comic, breaking realism rather than embarrassing anyone (The Young Ones, The Mighty Boosh, Get a Life, Joe Pera Talks With You). A surreal sketch show goes to B8-13.
leaves.see: B8-13 Sketch Comedy; B8-19 Fantasy Sitcom
leaves.axis: by the break with realism: British alternative comedy first, then absurdist narrative comedy; anti-comedy last

leaves.label: Sketch Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series made of short unrelated sketches, with recurring characters but no running plot (Monty Python's Flying Circus, Saturday Night Live, The Fast Show, Key & Peele). A sketch series for children goes to B10-3.
leaves.see: B8-12 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy; B15 Variety & Talk Formats; B10-3 Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy
leaves.axis: by the format: the variety-sketch show first, then live ensembles, troupes, character showcases, star vehicles, topical satire; prank, puppet and riffing shows last

leaves.label: Ramadan Comedy
leaves.defn: An Arabic-language comedy series made for the Ramadan prime-time season, typically thirty episodes, often social satire (Maraya, Tash ma Tash, Choufli Hal, El Kebeer Awi). Ramadan drama goes to B12.
leaves.see: B12 Serial Drama Traditions; B8-15 Political Satire

leaves.label: Political Satire
leaves.defn: A comedy series that ridicules power: governments, politicians, news media, bureaucracy, monarchy or the rich (Yes Minister, The Thick of It, Veep, Brass Eye).
leaves.see: B8-16 Parody Series; B8-13 Sketch Comedy; B15 Variety & Talk Formats
leaves.axis: by the target: government first, then the news media, bureaucracy and corporations, monarchy and history; society at large last

leaves.label: Parody Series
leaves.defn: A comedy series that imitates and mocks a specific genre or programme (Police Squad!, Sledge Hammer!, Childrens Hospital, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace). A documentary-form parody goes to B8-11.
leaves.see: B8-11 Mockumentary; B8-15 Political Satire
leaves.axis: by the genre mocked: cop shows first, then spy, action and superhero, fantasy and horror, soaps and melodrama; film and media spoofs last

leaves.label: Musical Comedy Series
leaves.defn: A comedy series in which characters perform songs as part of the story (Flight of the Conchords, Glee, Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, Schmigadoon!).
leaves.see: A14 Musical & Dance Film; B8-24 Comedy-Drama

leaves.label: Sports Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series set around a team, athlete or sport, built on competition and locker-room egos (Coach, Eastbound & Down, Ted Lasso, Shoresy).
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; B11-7 Sports Documentary Series

leaves.label: Fantasy Sitcom
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose premise is a magical, supernatural or impossible element placed in everyday life (Bewitched, ALF, 3rd Rock from the Sun, The Good Place). Spaceships and future worlds go to B8-20; ghosts and monsters played for scares to B8-21.
leaves.see: B8-20 Science Fiction Comedy; B8-21 Horror Comedy; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the impossible element: magic and supernatural beings first, then aliens, robots and creatures, afterlife and high-concept premises; body-swap and time-slip last

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series set in space, the future or a technological world (Hyperdrive, Avenue 5, Upload, The Last Man on Earth).
leaves.see: B8-19 Fantasy Sitcom; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Horror Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series built on horror premises (ghosts, vampires, zombies, slashers) played for laughs (Santa Clarita Diet, Ghosts, Scream Queens, Stan Against Evil).
leaves.see: B8-19 Fantasy Sitcom; B9 Speculative Series; A4 Horror

leaves.label: Crime Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is crime: criminals, cons, heists, comic cops or murder mysteries played for laughs (Porridge, Weeds, Los simuladores, The Afterparty). A parody of cop shows goes to B8-16; a crime drama to B7.
leaves.see: B7 Crime & Thriller Series; B8-23 Black Comedy; B8-16 Parody Series
leaves.axis: by the side of the law: criminals, cons and heists first, then comic detectives and police; comic murder mysteries last

leaves.label: Black Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series that finds humour in death, cruelty, despair or taboo, inviting laughter at the dreadful (Nighty Night, Inside No. 9, Barry, Dead to Me).
leaves.see: B8-22 Crime Comedy; B8-25 Tragicomedy

leaves.label: Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A series that balances comedy with dramatic stakes and serialized character arcs, usually single-camera and hour or half-hour (Northern Exposure, Gilmore Girls, Sex and the City, Atlanta). Comedy built on illness, grief or crisis goes to B8-25; a drama with light touches to B1.
leaves.see: B8-25 Tragicomedy; B1 Drama Series; B8-6 Romantic Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by the subject: family first, then small towns, professions, workplaces and the arts, women's ensembles, the comedian's own life; anthologies last

leaves.label: Tragicomedy
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama whose comedy is wrung from a wound: terminal illness, bereavement, addiction, mental illness or midlife collapse (The Big C, After Life, Kidding, Mom).
leaves.see: B8-24 Comedy-Drama; B8-23 Black Comedy
leaves.axis: by the wound: illness and dying first, then grief, addiction and mental health; divorce and midlife crisis last

subs.label: Children's Series
subs.axis: Axis: by age and mode: preschool first, then educational, sketch, sitcom and drama for older children, realistic and fantastic adventure; the seasonal Christmas calendar last

leaves.label: Preschool Television
leaves.defn: A live-action or puppet series made for children under about six, teaching through song, repetition and play (Sesame Street, Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, Teletubbies, Blue's Clues). Animated preschool series go to C13.
leaves.see: B10-2 Educational Children's Series; C13 Animated Series

leaves.label: Educational Children's Series
leaves.defn: A school-age children's series whose purpose is teaching reading, science or history, often with a presenter (The Electric Company, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy, Blue Peter).
leaves.see: B10-1 Preschool Television; B10-3 Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy

leaves.label: Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series for children made of sketches, puppet routines or variety segments rather than a single story (You Can't Do That on Television, All That, Pee-wee's Playhouse, 31 Minutes).
leaves.see: B8-13 Sketch Comedy; B10-1 Preschool Television

leaves.label: Teen Sitcom
leaves.defn: A sitcom made for children's networks about tweens and teens at school, at home or in showbusiness (Saved by the Bell, Lizzie McGuire, Hannah Montana, iCarly). A teen comedy for adults goes to B8-7.
leaves.aliases: tween sitcom; kidcom; Disney Channel / Nickelodeon sitcom
leaves.see: B8-7 Teen Comedy; B10-5 Teen Drama
leaves.axis: by the premise: school and everyday life first, then family and siblings, showbusiness and double lives, magic and superpowers; hotels and camps last

leaves.label: Teen Drama
leaves.defn: A serialized live-action drama or dramedy made for children's networks about teens: sport, dance, friendship and growing up (Andi Mack, The Next Step, Free Rein, Geek Girl). Teen drama for adults goes to B1.
leaves.see: B10-4 Teen Sitcom; B1 Drama Series

leaves.label: Children's Adventure Series
leaves.defn: A live-action children's series of realistic adventure: animal companions, literary classics and kid-gang mysteries (Lassie, Pippi Longstocking, Emil of Lönneberga, De Zevensprong). Magic and science fiction go to B10-7.
leaves.see: B10-7 Children's Fantasy Series; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the source of adventure: an animal companion first, then a literary classic; kid-gang and detective adventures last

leaves.label: Children's Fantasy Series
leaves.defn: A live-action children's series built on magic, the supernatural, science fiction or horror (Arabela, Round the Twist, The Worst Witch, Goosebumps).
leaves.see: B10-6 Children's Adventure Series; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the impossible element: fairy-tale magic in everyday life first, then magic schools and supernatural teens, science fiction and superheroes; horror anthologies last

leaves.label: Christmas Calendar
leaves.defn: A Nordic television serial of 24 episodes broadcast daily from 1 to 24 December (Jul i Skomakergata, Nissebanden, Sunes jul); adult parodies of the form (The Julekalender) stay here.
leaves.see: B10-7 Children's Fantasy Series

subs.label: Documentary Series
subs.axis: Axis: by subject: the natural world and science first, then history and war, lives, music, sport and the arts, travel and food, investigation; true crime and the paranormal last

leaves.label: Nature Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about animals, plants and ecosystems, including reconstructions of prehistoric life (Life on Earth, Planet Earth, Blue Planet II, Walking with Dinosaurs).
leaves.see: B11-2 Science Documentary Series
leaves.axis: by approach: the landmark global series first, then the Attenborough "Life" surveys, regional portraits, presenter-led wildlife; prehistoric reconstructions last

leaves.label: Science Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series explaining science, space, the body or how things work (Cosmos: A Personal Voyage, NOVA, How the Universe Works, Explained).
leaves.see: B11-1 Nature Documentary Series; B10-2 Educational Children's Series
leaves.axis: by subject: the cosmos first, then general science strands; explainer and pop-science formats last

leaves.label: History Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series narrating past events, eras or peoples (other than war), from archive narration to docudrama (American Experience, Prohibition, The Century of the Self, Mayday). War history goes to B11-4.
leaves.see: B11-4 War Documentary Series; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by method: narrative national history first, then social and cultural history, docudrama hybrids, essay and polemic; disaster and event retrospectives last

leaves.label: War Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about a war or the military history of an era (The World at War, The Civil War, The Vietnam War, Apocalypse: The Second World War).
leaves.see: B11-3 History Documentary Series; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Biographical Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series portraying the life of a person (other than athletes and musicians) through archive and interview (Biography, The Roosevelts, Arnold, Harry & Meghan). Athletes go to B11-7; musicians to B11-6.
leaves.see: B11-6 Music Documentary Series; B11-7 Sports Documentary Series; A11 Biographical Film
leaves.axis: by subject: entertainers first, then politicians, royals and business figures; artists and writers last

leaves.label: Music Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about musicians, genres or music scenes (The Beatles Anthology, Jazz, Hip Hop Evolution, The Beatles: Get Back).
leaves.see: B11-5 Biographical Documentary Series; A14 Musical & Dance Film

leaves.label: Sports Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about athletes, teams or sporting events (30 for 30, The Last Dance, Formula 1: Drive to Survive, Last Chance U). Live sport goes to B16.
leaves.see: B16 Live Event & Sports Television; B11-5 Biographical Documentary Series
leaves.axis: by time: all-access season followed as it happens first; retrospectives and athlete portraits last

leaves.label: Arts & Pop-Culture Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about art, design, film, television, toys or pop culture, including making-of series (Civilisation, The Story of Film: An Odyssey, The Toys That Made Us, LIGHT & MAGIC).
leaves.see: B11-5 Biographical Documentary Series; B11-6 Music Documentary Series

leaves.label: Travel & Food Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A non-competitive documentary series following a presenter through places or cuisines (Michael Palin: Around the World in 80 Days, An Idiot Abroad, Chef's Table, Street Food: Asia). Cooking competitions go to B13.
leaves.see: B13 Competition Formats; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats
leaves.axis: by approach: classic travelogues first, then comic and celebrity travelogues; food and culinary documentary last

leaves.label: Investigative & Observational Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series exposing wrongdoing or observing an institution or community from inside, and the anthology strands that carry such films (Dirty Money, Rotten, Hopkins, POV). Criminal cases go to B11-11.
leaves.aliases: exposé series; fly-on-the-wall documentary; documentary strand
leaves.see: B11-11 True Crime Docuseries; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats
leaves.axis: by method: investigative exposé first, then observational access; anthology strands last

leaves.label: True Crime Docuseries
leaves.defn: A documentary series reconstructing a real crime, investigation or trial (Making a Murderer, The Jinx, Tiger King, Forensic Files). A dramatized true-crime series goes to B7.
leaves.see: B11-10 Investigative & Observational Documentary Series; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the crime: the single murder case first, then serial killers, wrongful conviction and trials, cults and abuse, fraud and cons, organised crime and terror; case-of-the-week strands last

leaves.label: Paranormal & Pseudo-Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A series in documentary form about hauntings, aliens or lost civilisations, presenting fringe claims as investigation (Ancient Aliens, Paranormal Witness, Ancient Apocalypse).
leaves.see: B11-3 History Documentary Series; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats
